import pandas as pd

# Find the players from Georgia and Penn State
georgia_pos = df.loc[df['school / club team'].str.strip().str.lower() == 'georgia', 'position']
penn_pos = df.loc[df['school / club team'].str.strip().str.lower() == 'penn state', 'position']

# Collect the individual positions from each player (positions may be combined like "guard / forward")
georgia_positions = set()
for p in georgia_pos:
    georgia_positions.update(x.strip().lower() for x in str(p).split('/'))

penn_positions = set()
for p in penn_pos:
    penn_positions.update(x.strip().lower() for x in str(p).split('/'))

# All distinct positions across the two players
all_positions = georgia_positions | penn_positions
# Positions shared by both players
shared_positions = georgia_positions & penn_positions

# The claim: there are three different positions in total, and the two players
# (from Georgia and Penn State) share two of the same... i.e., they share a position
# among the three distinct positions listed.
answer = bool(len(all_positions) == 3 and len(shared_positions) >= 1)
